messages.subject: Derive 2D parameter from 3D array
parts:
Hello everyone,

I would like to derive a 2D parameter from a 3D arrays, and I am having issues wrapping my head around dimensions.

Essentially, I have pairwise comparisons of individuals born in different years (b1 and b2). I am using the probability that some of them are half-siblings (y_array) to estimate demographic parameters, through a binomial distribution: y_array ~ dbinom (prob, size_array). I also have to integrate over a third dimension: the age of the shared parent at b1 and b2. So my arrays have 3 dimensions [b1, b2, age] with:

b1= c(40:59)
b2 = c(40:59)
age = c(1:20)

As you can see, b1 and b2 both refer to the same variable "year" , except that b1 corresponds to birth year of ind1 and b2 corresponds to birth year of ind2 (which is always at least one year later).

My challenge is that I would like to derive a 2D parameter TRO [b,age] with a unique value for each year and age combination. The code below does not work because I have multiple definitions for TRO (multiple b2's looped for each [b1,age]).

I first wanted to derive TRO outside of the b2 loop, but then I also loose the indexing for age. Is there a simple way to average the b2's that correspond to group [b1, age]?

library(nimble)
# Load the Rdata file

model <- nimbleCode({
 
  # priors
  Nm ~ dunif(0, 20000)
  lambda ~ dunif(-0.5, 0.5) # Uniform prior for population growth.
 
  # likelihoods
 
  for (b1 in 1:hsp_dad_length_b1){ # For each row of the array (b1)
   
    for (b2 in (b1+1):hsp_dad_length_b2){ # For each column of the array (b2). The i+1 makes sure that we're only doing comparisons where b1<b2 (right side of the diagonal of the array)
     
      for (age in 3:(max.age - dad_age_gap[b1,b2])){ # For each possible age
       
        y_array[b1,b2,age] ~ dbinom(((RO[age] / TRO [b1,age]) * # TRO at b1
                                       (RO[age+dad_age_gap[b1,b2]] / TRO [b2,age+dad_age_gap[b1,b2]])), # TRO at b2
                                     size_array[b1,b2,age]) # All comparisons
       
        # Derived parameter TRO for each year and age
        TRO[b1,age] <- RO[age] * Nm * exp(lambda * (hsp_dad_unique_b1[b1] - estimation_year))
        
      } # age
    } # b2
  } # b1

TRO[1: hsp_dad_length_b1, 1:2] <- 0 # Fix TRO at 0 for ages 1 and 2

})

my.constants <- list(
  hsp_dad_length_b1 = nrow(y_array),
  hsp_dad_length_b2 = ncol(y_array),
  dad_age_gap = gap_array,
  hsp_dad_unique_b1 = as.numeric(rownames(y_array)),
  #hsp_dad_unique_b2 = as.numeric(colnames(y_array)),
  RO = RO,
  estimation_year = 58,
  max.age = 20
)

my.data <- list(
  y_array <- y_array,
  size_array = size_array
)

initial.values <- function() list(Nm = rnorm(1, mean = 5000, sd = 1000),
                                  lambda = rnorm(1, mean = 0, sd = 0.05),

parameters.to.save <- c("Nm", "lambda", "TRO")

n.iter <- 50000
n.burnin <- 5000
n.chains <- 2
n.thin <- 1

mcmc.output <- nimbleMCMC(code = model,
                          constants = my.constants,
                          data = my.data,
                          inits = initial.values,
                          monitors = parameters.to.save,
                          niter = n.iter,
                          thin = n.thin,
                          nburnin = n.burnin,
                          nchains = n.chains)

I attached the RData file for the reproducible example. I hope everything is clear.

Thanks!!

Anthony

messages.subject: Re: Derive 2D parameter from 3D array
parts:
Hi Anthony, 

I think in order to make this work, the variable TRO needs to go into a separate time-loop. Since the ranges for b1 and b2 are the same, we only need to define TRO for the common range (let's call it b, 1:20) and for the age range 3:20 (20 = maximum age gap + 1). 
The below seems to work:

model <- nimbleCode({
 
  # priors
  Nm ~ dunif(0, 20000)
  lambda ~ dunif(-0.5, 0.5)

# likelihoods

  for (b1 in 1:(my.constants$hsp_dad_length_b1-1)){ #* Added -1 to avoid b2 loop going beyond available space
for (b2 in (b1+1):hsp_dad_length_b2){
for (age in 3:(max.age - dad_age_gap[b1,b2])){

y_array[b1,b2,age] ~ dbinom((RO[age] / TRO[b1,age]) *
                                    (RO[age+dad_age_gap[b1,b2]] / TRO[b2,age+dad_age_gap[b1,b2]]),
                                    size_array[b1,b2,age])

}
    }
  }

 
  TRO[1:hsp_dad_length_b1, 1:2] <- 0 #

#* Separate loop for calculating TRO
  for (b in 1:hsp_dad_length_b1){
   
      for (age in 3:(dad_age_gap_max+1)){ #* Changed loop definition to cover all values for age (gap)
# Derived parameter TRO for each year and age
TRO[b,age] <- RO[age] * Nm * exp(lambda * (hsp_dad_unique_b1[b] - estimation_year))

}
  }
 
})

my.constants <- list(
  hsp_dad_length_b1 = nrow(y_array),
  hsp_dad_length_b2 = ncol(y_array),
  dad_age_gap = gap_array,
dad_age_gap_max = max(abs(gap_array)), #* Added new variable

RO = RO,
  estimation_year = 58,
  max.age = 20
)

my.data <- list(

y_array = y_array,
  size_array = size_array,
  hsp_dad_unique_b1 = as.numeric(rownames(y_array)) #* Moved into data to allow dynamic indexing

)

initial.values <- function() list(Nm = rnorm(1, mean = 5000, sd = 1000),
lambda = rnorm(1, mean = 0, sd = 0.05))
parameters.to.save <- c("Nm", "lambda", "TRO")

n.iter <- 10
n.burnin <- 0
n.chains <- 1

n.thin <- 1

mcmc.output <- nimbleMCMC(code = model,
                          constants = my.constants,
                          data = my.data,
                          inits = initial.values,
                          monitors = parameters.to.save,
                          niter = n.iter,
                          thin = n.thin,
                          nburnin = n.burnin,
                          nchains = n.chains)

I defined a new variable "dad_age_gap_max" to define the range for TRO, moved hsp_dad_unique_b1 into data to allow dynamic indexing (does not work for constants currently), and changed the data likelihood definition to not go beyond the dimensions of your arrays (with b2 = b1+1). I've marked all changes with #* in the code above. 
Please check this carefully though, as I do not fully understand your setup and may have implemented indexing that is not correct in context. 

Note that this solution works as long as hsp_dad_length_b1 == hsp_dad_length_b2 (i.e. your arrays are symmetric). 
If you have asymmetric arrays, I think you would have to define two variables TRO_1b and TRO_b2, still in their own loops though.
